# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind monkey. I can only touch the bomb and feel its components, but I cannot see colors or read text. The manual is held by Mute, who can speak to me. Deaf can see the bomb's visual details (colors, markings) but cannot hear or touch.

My primary goal is to get information from Mute about what the manual says regarding the wires, and potentially coordinate with Deaf through Mute if necessary, though direct communication between Deaf and Mute is limited (Deaf sees gestures from Mute, Mute hears nothing). However, Mute speaks to me. Deaf gestures to... well, Deaf can gesture to anyone who can see. Mute can see. I cannot see. So Deaf can communicate visually to Mute.

Let's establish contact with Mute first. I need to know what the manual says about the three wires. Since I don't know their state yet, I'll ask for general instructions or descriptions of the wire types/positions if the manual describes them abstractly, or simply ask "What do I do?"

However, the most efficient path is usually:
1. Ask Mute for instructions based on the manual.
2. If the manual requires color info, ask Mute to signal Deaf? No, Mute can't speak to Deaf effectively if Deaf can't hear, and Mute can't gesture if he's reading? Wait, Mute *can* gesture. The rules say Mute "Cannot Speak". But Mute *can* Read Manual. Can Mute Gesture? Yes, "A gesture is made with the hands... Whoever can see receives it". Mute has hands. Deaf can see. So Mute can gesture to Deaf. Deaf can see the bomb. Deaf can gesture back to Mute. Mute can read the manual and interpret Deaf's gestures. Then Mute tells me (Blind) what to do via speech.

So the chain is: Me -> Mute (Speech) -> Mute interprets Manual -> Mute gestures to Deaf -> Deaf looks at bomb -> Deaf gestures to Mute -> Mute reads gesture + Manual -> Mute tells me (Speech) -> I act.

This is complex. Let's start simple. I will ask Mute what the manual says about the wires in general terms, or specifically what action to take if there are no conditions, or what information is needed.

Actually, I should just ask Mute: "What does the manual say about the wires?"

```
speak(to="mute", text="what does the manual say about the wires")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The display shows 0. The light is red. There are three wires: number 1 is blue, number 2 is green, and number 3 is red.

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: The light is now WHITE. The display still shows 0. Wires are unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.

I am the Blind monkey. I have received information from Deaf about the bomb's visual state:
- Display: 0
- Light: White (changed from Red)
- Wires: 1 is Blue, 2 is Green, 3 is Red.

However, I cannot see these colors or markings myself. My view only shows `[?]` for everything because I can't perceive them without touch, and color/text are not tactile properties in this context (or at least, I haven't been told they are). The prompt says "Anything merely printed or painted is not there for you". So I know *that* there are wires, but I don't know their colors unless someone tells me. Deaf has just told me.

Now I need to consult the Manual via Mute. Mute can read the manual. I should ask Mute what the instructions are for a bomb with a white light, display 0, and wires Blue/Green/Red. Since Mute speaks to me, I can convey this info to Mute? No, Mute cannot hear Deaf. But I can speak to Mute. I can tell Mute what Deaf said.

So, I will speak to Mute, providing the visual details so Mute can look up the correct action in the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="the light is white, the display shows 0, and the wires are blue green red")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Hypothesis: Cut the wire whose color matches the current light. The light is currently GREEN. Wire 2 is GREEN. Please cut Wire 2.

```
speak(to="mute", text="deaf says light is green and wire 2 is green. manual rule for white light display 0?")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The light is now RED. Based on the previous cycle, if the rule is 'cut the wire matching the light color', you should now cut WIRE 3 (which is red). Please proceed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="light is red. wire 3 is red. manual rule?")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The light is WHITE. There is no white wire. Based on the 'cut matching color' hypothesis, do NOT cut any wire right now. Wait for the light to turn Red or Green.

```
speak(to="mute", text="light is white. no white wire. manual rule?")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The light is GREEN. The Mute is signaling specifically for Wire 2. Please cut WIRE 2 (green).
